# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

### I. LOOP-DRAWING GAMES
*Objective: Draw a single continuous, non-crossing, non-branching loop*

#### A. Unconstrained Path
- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbers indicate how many sides of a cell are used

#### B. Cell-Passing with Circle Constraints
- **Masyu** — Loop must pass through all circles; black circles require turns, white circles require straight paths
- **Mid-loop** — Loop must pass through all black circles, with each circle as the midpoint of a straight segment

#### C. Region-Based Loop Rules
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through each bold-lined room once; must alternate between moon-only and sun-only rooms
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop passes through white circles; within each bold-lined area, all white circles are either all straight or all turning

#### D. Directional/Wind-Constrained Loops
- **Nagareru** — Loop direction is fixed by arrows in black cells; wind from black cells constrains movement direction
- **Suraromu** — Loop starts and ends at numbered circle; must pass through all "Gates" exactly once in a specified order

#### E. Loop with Black Cell Constraints
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells and numbered cells; arrow-numbers indicate count of black cells in a direction
- **Masyu** *(also listed above)*

---

### II. PATH / CONNECTION GAMES
*Objective: Connect elements or trace paths without forming a full loop*

#### A. Island Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges (max 2 per pair); all islands must be connected

#### B. Number Pair Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-overlapping lines that fill all cells

#### C. Circle/Token Movement
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles horizontally/vertically into their home country; numbered circles move exact distances
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles straight into gray areas; gray area numbers must match sum of entering circles

---

### III. REGION-DIVISION GAMES
*Objective: Partition the grid into defined regions*

#### A. Rectangle/Square Regions
- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number indicating its cell count

#### B. Fixed-Size Polyomino Regions
- **Five Cells** — Divide into pentominoes (blocks of exactly 5 cells); numbers indicate boundary line count around a cell
- **LITS** — Color one tetromino per bold-lined area; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch; colored cells must be connected

#### C. Variable-Size Numbered Regions
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbered blocks; each block's size equals its number; same-size blocks cannot touch
- **Ripple Effect** — Fill rooms with consecutive numbers from 1; duplicate numbers in a row/column must be separated by distance ≥ that number

#### D. L-Shaped Regions
- **Sashigane** — Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark the knee (bend); arrows point toward the knee

#### E. Paired/Mirrored Regions
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing equal white and gray areas of identical shape (rotation/mirror allowed)
- **Nuritwin** — Each bold-lined region contains exactly two same-size shaded blocks that don't touch; all shaded cells connect globally

#### F. Color-Matched Regions
- **Choco Banana** — Black cells form rectangles/squares; white cells do NOT form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate area size

---

### IV. CELL-SHADING / PAINTING GAMES
*Objective: Determine which cells to color black (or shade)*

#### A. Shading with Connectivity Rules
- **Nurikabe** — White cell islands have numbered sizes; black cells form one connected wall; no 2×2 black squares
- **Heyawake** — Rooms have numbered black cell counts; black cells cannot touch; white cells cannot span more than two rooms in a line
- **Kurodoko** — Numbers indicate total white cells visible from that cell (horizontally + vertically); black cells cannot touch
- **Kurotto** — Circles show the sum of connected black cells extending from them; circled cells stay white
- **Usowan** — Numbers show adjacent black cell count, but exactly one number per bold-lined room is deliberately wrong; black cells cannot touch

#### B. Shading with Structural Shape Rules
- **Norinori** — Place dominoes (pairs of black cells) so each bold-lined area contains exactly two black cells
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms per given counts; when "dropped" downward, shaded cells fill the bottom half exactly
- **Nurimeizu** — Paint rooms entirely black or white to create a maze from S to G; circles on shortest path, triangles off it; no 2×2 uniformity

#### C. Shading with Triangle Placement
- **Shakashaka** — Place black triangles in cells so remaining white space always forms rectangles/squares; numbers count adjacent triangles

#### D. Shading with Tile Constraints
- **Tilepaint** — Color entire "tile" regions; diagonal-numbered cells indicate black cell counts in their row/column segment; solution reveals an image

#### E. Shading Derived from Number Logic
- **Hitori** — Shade cells so no number repeats in any row/column; shaded cells cannot touch; white cells stay connected

---

### V. NUMBER-PLACEMENT GAMES
*Objective: Fill cells with numbers according to logical constraints*

#### A. Latin-Square / Uniqueness Constraints
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box with no repeats

#### B. Room-Based Number Filling
- **Makaro** — Each bold-lined room contains numbers 1 to (room size); arrow-black cells indicate which neighbor holds the maximum; no same number adjacent across rooms

#### C. Cross-Referential Number Filling
- **Nansuke** — Fill white cells with digits forming numbers from a given list; numbers read horizontally or vertically

#### D. Snake/Sequential Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes cannot share sides; directional visibility rules restrict where other snakes can appear relative to a snake's "view"

#### E. Symbol Fill (Non-Numeric)
- **Juosan** — Fill all cells with — or |; territory numbers indicate the difference in counts; marks cannot extend in the perpendicular direction beyond two cells

---

### VI. BLOCK-PATTERN GAMES
*Objective: Identify, place, or chain defined black-cell blocks*

#### A. Chain-Constrained Blocks
- **Chained Block** — Consecutive black cells form blocks with size numbers; all blocks must form corner-touching chains; no two same-shaped blocks in one chain

---

### VII. HYBRID / MULTI-MECHANIC GAMES
*Games combining shading, region logic, and path or placement elements*

#### A. Light/Visibility Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells indicate adjacent bulb count; every white cell must be illuminated; bulbs cannot illuminate each other

#### B. Promontory / White Cell Shading
- **Nurimisaki** — Circled cells are "Misaki" (promontories) with exactly one white neighbor; numbers indicate white cell line length from Misaki; white cells connected; no 2×2 uniformity

#### C. Shape-Growing Sequences (Evolomino)
- **Evolomino** — Draw squares in cells to form blocks; each block contains one arrow; each successive block along an arrow's route adds exactly one cell to the previous block's shape without rotation or flipping

#### D. Pencil-Line Tracing
- **Pencils** — Identify pencil bodies (straight groups of cells) with a tip; draw a line from the tip through as many cells as the pencil's number; lines cannot cross or branch

---

## Summary Cross-Reference Table

| Category | Key Distinguishing Feature | Games |
|---|---|---|
| Loop Drawing | Single closed path | Slitherlink, Masyu, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Nagareru, Suraromu, Yajilin |
| Path/Connection | Open paths or token movement | Hashiwokakero, Numberlink, Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
| Region Division | Partitioning grid into defined zones | Shikaku, Five Cells, LITS, Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Sashigane, Double Choco, Nuritwin, Choco Banana |
| Cell Shading | Determining black/white cell status | Nurikabe, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Usowan, Norinori, Sto-stone, Nurimeizu, Shakashaka, Tilepaint, Hitori |
| Number Placement | Filling cells with digits | Sudoku, Makaro, Nansuke, Hebi, Juosan |
| Block Patterns | Rules about contiguous black-cell groups | Chained Block |
| Hybrid | Multiple simultaneous mechanics | Akari, Nurimisaki, Evolomino, Pencils |
